//cleanUrls: MUST stay false now that the Supabase-backed social app ships here. Vercel's cleanUrls strips the .html extension and 308-redirects /faero_v1_launch.html -> /faero_v1_launch. Supabase matches auth redirect URLs EXACTLY, so that redirect silently breaks password reset and email confirmation. It also makes the service worker's offline fallback miss (it looks up 'faero_v1_launch.html') and puts a redirect in front of the PWA start_url on every launch. The OS itself is unaffected: index.html is served at '/' natively and the app registry uses explicit .html paths.
//frame: X-Frame-Options is SAMEORIGIN, not DENY, and frame-ancestors is 'self', not 'none'. This is deliberate and load-bearing: the faero OS opens the social app in an iframe window, and DENY / 'none' block same-origin framing too — they would break the desktop integration outright while looking like a pure security win. SAMEORIGIN still blocks third-party clickjacking, which is the actual threat.
//csp: Only frame-ancestors is enforced for now. A full CSP (script-src / connect-src / frame-src) is NOT shipped here, and that is a known, deliberate gap rather than an oversight: this origin also serves ~20 legacy OS apps that load from cdn.emulatorjs.org, unpkg.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, stream.zeno.fm, 00s.myretrotvs.com, api.dicebear.com, youtube, twitch, mixcloud and soundcloud. A restrictive policy written without testing each of those would break them silently. frame-ancestors alone is safe to enforce because it constrains who may frame this site, not what it may load. See DEPLOY.md 'Remaining hardening'.

headers.//: The two shells must never be cached hard, or a deploy leaves users on stale code. This overrides the s-maxage above for these paths.
